neighbours.label: being next to something: ' neighboring' / ' neighbor' / 'next door' / 'bordering' (adjacency between places or parties)
fire: Smoke from the warehouse drifted over the neighboring streets all afternoon.
The farmers sell most of their cheese in the neighbouring valley.
When the power failed, we borrowed candles from the couple next door.
The bakery shares a wall with the bookshop next door.
Trade with the bordering provinces doubled after the road was paved.
The children were not allowed to play with the neighbor's dog.
The treaty settled a long dispute with the neighboring kingdom.
Water from the burst pipe leaked into the neighbouring flat.
quiet: Smoke from the warehouse drifted over the empty streets all afternoon.
The farmers sell most of their cheese in the distant capital.
When the power failed, we borrowed candles from the couple we met last year.
The bakery shares a van with the bookshop on delivery days.
Trade with the far provinces doubled after the road was paved.
The children were not allowed to play with the stray dog.
The treaty settled a long dispute with the rival kingdom, and next year the king will visit.
Water from the burst pipe leaked into the ground floor.

notes: Card: ' neighboring' x7, ' next' (door) x3, ' neighbor', ' neighbouring', ' adjacent', ' across' (the border); the + direction suppresses ' neighbor', ' nearby', ' adjacent', ' adjoining', so this pole writes them. The + pole is the other side: what holds within one whole (unity of, coherence between, binds; promotes ' within', ' inside'). Probes: neighboring 0.56, next door 0.60, bordering 0.59, adjacent 0.19; same sentences without adjacency < 0.10. Near misses include 'next' without adjacency and 'far' / 'distant'.
